questions.figure: Graph: line y = x cutting the parabola y = x<sup>2</sup> − x (vertex (0.5, −0.25)) at the origin and at (2, 2).

questions.question: Find the equation, in the form y = ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c, of the parabola which cuts the x-axis at (1, 0) and (5, 0) and cuts the y-axis at (0, 15).
questions.explanation: The x-intercepts give y = a(x − 1)(x − 5). The y-intercept (0, 15) gives 15 = a(0 − 1)(0 − 5) = 5a, so a = 3. Hence y = 3(x − 1)(x − 5) = 3(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 5) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 18x + 15.

questions.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c. Given that f(0) = 5, f(−1) = 15 and f(1) = 1, find the values of a, b and c.
questions.explanation: f(0) = 5 gives c = 5. f(−1) = a − b + 5 = 15 ⇒ a − b = 10. f(1) = a + b + 5 = 1 ⇒ a + b = −4. Adding: 2a = 6 ⇒ a = 3; then b = −4 − 3 = −7. So f(x) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 7x + 5.

questions.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 5. Find the values of x for which f(x) = f(3).
questions.explanation: f(3) = 9 − 9 + 5 = 5. Set x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 5 = 5 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 3x = 0 ⇒ x(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 or x = 3.

questions.question: Solve the inequality 2x + 5 < 9, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, and represent the solution on the number line in each case.
questions.explanation: 2x + 5 < 9 ⇒ 2x < 9 − 5 ⇒ 2x < 4 ⇒ x < 2. On the number line put a hollow (open) circle at 2, because x = 2 is excluded by the strict inequality, and draw a heavy arrow from it towards the left; every point of the shaded ray satisfies the inequality.

questions.question: Solve the inequality 3x − 1 > 10, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, and represent the solution on the number line in each case.
questions.explanation: 3x − 1 > 10 ⇒ 3x > 11 ⇒ x > 11/3 (≈ 3.67). On the number line put a hollow circle at 11/3 and draw a heavy arrow from it towards the right; all numbers greater than 11/3 satisfy the inequality.

questions.question: Solve the inequality 4x − 5 ≤ 3 + 2x, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, and represent the solution on the number line in each case.
questions.explanation: 4x − 5 ≤ 3 + 2x ⇒ 4x − 2x ≤ 3 + 5 ⇒ 2x ≤ 8 ⇒ x ≤ 4. On the number line put a solid (filled) dot at 4, because x = 4 is included (≤), and draw a heavy arrow from it towards the left.

questions.question: Solve the inequality 6 < 3(x + 2) < 21, ∀ x ∈ ℝ, and represent the solution on the number line in each case.
questions.explanation: Divide all three parts by 3: 2 < x + 2 < 7. Subtract 2 from each part: 0 < x < 5. On the number line put hollow circles at 0 and at 5 and thicken the segment between them; the endpoints are excluded, so the solution is the open interval (0, 5).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the linear inequality 2x − y ≤ 7.
questions.answer: Boundary line 2x − y = 7 through (7/2, 0) and (0, −7); the solution region is the half-plane y ≥ 2x − 7 (the side containing the origin), boundary included.
questions.explanation: For the boundary 2x − y = 7: putting y = 0 gives x = 7/2, and putting x = 0 gives y = −7, so the line passes through (7/2, 0) and (0, −7). Draw it as a solid line because ≤ includes the boundary. Test the origin O(0, 0): 2(0) − 0 = 0 ≤ 7 is true, so O lies in the solution region; shade the half-plane containing O, i.e. the region above the line (y ≥ 2x − 7).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the linear inequality 3x + 4y ≥ 10.
questions.answer: Boundary line 3x + 4y = 10 through (10/3, 0) and (0, 5/2); the solution region is the half-plane above the line (the side away from the origin), boundary included.
questions.explanation: For 3x + 4y = 10: y = 0 gives x = 10/3, x = 0 gives y = 5/2, so the line passes through (10/3, 0) and (0, 5/2). Draw a solid line. Test O(0, 0): 0 ≥ 10 is false, so the origin is not in the region; shade the half-plane on the other side of the line, i.e. above it.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the linear inequality x − 2y ≥ 5.
questions.answer: Boundary line x − 2y = 5 through (5, 0) and (0, −5/2); the solution region is the half-plane below the line (y ≤ (x − 5)/2), boundary included.
questions.explanation: For x − 2y = 5: y = 0 gives x = 5, x = 0 gives y = −5/2, so the line passes through (5, 0) and (0, −5/2). Draw a solid line. Test O(0, 0): 0 ≥ 5 is false, so the origin is not in the region; shade the other side, i.e. the half-plane below/right of the line, which is y ≤ (x − 5)/2.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the linear inequality 2x + y ≤ 4.
questions.answer: Boundary line 2x + y = 4 through (2, 0) and (0, 4); the solution region is the half-plane below the line (the side containing the origin), boundary included.
questions.explanation: For 2x + y = 4: y = 0 gives x = 2, x = 0 gives y = 4, so the line passes through (2, 0) and (0, 4). Draw a solid line. Test O(0, 0): 0 ≤ 4 is true, so the origin is in the region; shade the half-plane containing the origin, i.e. the region below/left of the line (y ≤ 4 − 2x).

questions.question: Solve the system of linear inequalities 3x − y ≥ 8 and 2x + 3y ≥ 5 graphically.
questions.answer: The solution region is the unbounded wedge lying below the line 3x − y = 8 and above the line 2x + 3y = 5; the two boundary lines meet at (29/11, −1/11) and the region opens to the right.
questions.explanation: Boundary 3x − y = 8 passes through (8/3, 0) and (0, −8); boundary 2x + 3y = 5 passes through (5/2, 0) and (0, 5/3). The origin fails both inequalities (0 ≥ 8 and 0 ≥ 5 are false), so for each line the half-plane away from O is taken: below 3x − y = 8, i.e. y ≤ 3x − 8, and above 2x + 3y = 5, i.e. y ≥ (5 − 2x)/3. The boundaries intersect where 2x + 3(3x − 8) = 5 ⇒ 11x = 29 ⇒ x = 29/11, y = 3(29/11) − 8 = −1/11. The common region is the angle with vertex (29/11, −1/11) ≈ (2.64, −0.09) opening to the right between the two boundary lines (both lines included); it is unbounded.

questions.question: Solve the system of linear inequalities 3x − 2y ≤ 6 and x − y ≤ 4 graphically.
questions.answer: The solution region is the unbounded region above both lines 3x − 2y = 6 and x − y = 4; the boundary lines meet at (−2, −6) and the region opens upwards.
questions.explanation: Boundary 3x − 2y = 6 passes through (2, 0) and (0, −3); boundary x − y = 4 passes through (4, 0) and (0, −4). The origin satisfies both (0 ≤ 6, 0 ≤ 4), so shade the half-plane containing O for each line: above 3x − 2y = 6 (y ≥ (3x − 6)/2) and above x − y = 4 (y ≥ x − 4). The boundaries meet where y = x − 4 and 3x − 2(x − 4) = 6 ⇒ x + 8 = 6 ⇒ x = −2, y = −6, giving the corner (−2, −6). The common region is the angle above both lines with vertex (−2, −6), unbounded upwards.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the solution region of the system 2x + y ≤ 5, 3x − 2y ≤ 7, x ≥ 0, and check whether the graph is bounded or not.
questions.answer: The solution region is the triangle with vertices (0, 5), (0, −7/2) and (17/7, 1/7); the graph is bounded.
questions.explanation: Boundary 2x + y = 5 cuts the axes at (5/2, 0) and (0, 5); boundary 3x − 2y = 7 cuts them at (7/3, 0) and (0, −7/2). The origin satisfies 2x + y ≤ 5 (0 ≤ 5), 3x − 2y ≤ 7 (0 ≤ 7) and x ≥ 0, so the region lies below the first line, above the second line and to the right of the y-axis. The two sloping boundaries meet where y = 5 − 2x and 3x − 2(5 − 2x) = 7 ⇒ 7x = 17 ⇒ x = 17/7, y = 1/7. On x = 0 the region runs from y = −7/2 up to y = 5. Hence the region is the closed triangle with vertices (0, 5), (0, −7/2) and (17/7, 1/7); since it is enclosed by three line segments, the graph is bounded.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the solution region of the system x + 2y ≤ 6, 2x − 3y ≥ 8, x + 2y ≤ 4, and check whether the graph is bounded or not.
questions.answer: The solution region is the unbounded wedge below both lines x + 2y = 4 and 2x − 3y = 8, with vertex (4, 0); the graph is not bounded.
questions.explanation: The condition x + 2y ≤ 4 is stricter than x + 2y ≤ 6, so the latter is redundant. Boundary x + 2y = 4 passes through (4, 0) and (0, 2); boundary 2x − 3y = 8 passes through (4, 0) and (0, −8/3). Since 2x − 3y ≥ 8 excludes the origin (0 ≥ 8 false), the region lies below 2x − 3y = 8, i.e. y ≤ (2x − 8)/3, and also below x + 2y = 4, i.e. y ≤ (4 − x)/2. The two lines meet at (4, 0). For x < 4 the boundary is 2x − 3y = 8, and for x > 4 it is x + 2y = 4, so the region is the downward-opening angle with vertex (4, 0): one arm is the ray of 2x − 3y = 8 through (0, −8/3), the other is the ray of x + 2y = 4 through (8, −2). It extends without limit downwards, so the graph is not bounded.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 2x − 3y ≤ 8, 3x + 2y ≤ 10, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the feasible region and the corner points.
questions.answer: Feasible region: the triangle with corner points (0, 0), (0, 5) and (10/3, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundary 2x − 3y = 8 has intercepts (4, 0) and (0, −8/3); boundary 3x + 2y = 10 has intercepts (10/3, 0) and (0, 5). The origin satisfies both inequalities (0 ≤ 8, 0 ≤ 10), so the feasible region is the part of the first quadrant below both lines. The line 2x − 3y = 8 passes below the first-quadrant triangle (at (10/3, 0) it gives 20/3 ≤ 8), so it does not cut the region. Hence the feasible region is the bounded triangle O(0, 0), (0, 5), (10/3, 0).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities −5x + 4y ≥ 10, 2x + y ≤ 8, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the feasible region and the corner points.
questions.answer: Feasible region: the triangle with corner points (0, 5/2), (0, 8) and (22/13, 60/13).
questions.explanation: Boundary −5x + 4y = 10, i.e. y = (10 + 5x)/4, has intercepts (0, 5/2) and (−2, 0); boundary 2x + y = 8 has intercepts (4, 0) and (0, 8). The origin fails the first inequality (0 ≥ 10 false), so the region lies above −5x + 4y = 10; it lies below 2x + y = 8 and in the first quadrant. The two boundary lines meet where y = 8 − 2x and −5x + 4(8 − 2x) = 10 ⇒ 32 − 13x = 10 ⇒ x = 22/13, y = 8 − 44/13 = 60/13. Hence the feasible region is the triangle (0, 5/2), (0, 8), (22/13, 60/13), which is bounded.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 4x + 3y ≤ 12, 3x − 2y ≤ 9, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the feasible region and the corner points.
questions.answer: Feasible region: the triangle with corner points (0, 0), (0, 4) and (3, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundary 4x + 3y = 12 has intercepts (3, 0) and (0, 4); boundary 3x − 2y = 9 has intercepts (3, 0) and (0, −9/2). The origin satisfies both (0 ≤ 12, 0 ≤ 9), so the region is below both lines in the first quadrant. Both boundary lines pass through (3, 0); the second line has negative y-intercept, so it leaves the first-quadrant triangle untouched. The feasible region is therefore the bounded triangle O(0, 0), (3, 0), (0, 4).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 5x − y ≤ 16, 3x + 2y ≤ 6, x + 2y ≤ 5, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the solution space and the corner points.
questions.answer: Solution space: the quadrilateral with corner points (0, 0), (0, 5/2), (1/2, 9/4) and (2, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundaries: 5x − y = 16 has intercepts (16/5, 0) and (0, −16); 3x + 2y = 6 has intercepts (2, 0) and (0, 3); x + 2y = 5 has intercepts (5, 0) and (0, 5/2). The origin satisfies all three (0 ≤ 16, 0 ≤ 6, 0 ≤ 5), so the region is below every line in the first quadrant. The binding lines are 3x + 2y = 6 and x + 2y = 5; they meet where, subtracting, 2x = 1 ⇒ x = 1/2 and y = (5 − 1/2)/2 = 9/4. The line 5x − y = 16 is slack (at (2, 0), 10 ≤ 16). The solution space is the bounded quadrilateral O(0, 0), (0, 5/2), (1/2, 9/4), (2, 0).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 5x + 3y ≤ 12, 2x − 3y ≤ 9, x + 2y ≤ 4, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the solution space and the corner points.
questions.answer: Solution space: the quadrilateral with corner points (0, 0), (0, 2), (12/7, 8/7) and (12/5, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundaries: 5x + 3y = 12 has intercepts (12/5, 0) and (0, 4); 2x − 3y = 9 has intercepts (9/2, 0) and (0, −3); x + 2y = 4 has intercepts (4, 0) and (0, 2). The origin satisfies all three, so the region is below every line in the first quadrant. The binding lines are 5x + 3y = 12 and x + 2y = 4; they meet where x = 4 − 2y and 5(4 − 2y) + 3y = 12 ⇒ 20 − 7y = 12 ⇒ y = 8/7, x = 12/7. The line 2x − 3y = 9 is slack (at (12/5, 0), 24/5 ≤ 9). The solution space is the bounded quadrilateral O(0, 0), (0, 2), (12/7, 8/7), (12/5, 0).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 6x + 5y ≥ 14, 4x + 2y ≤ 10, 3x − 2y ≤ 8, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and identify the solution space and the corner points.
questions.answer: Solution space: the quadrilateral with corner points (0, 14/5), (0, 5), (5/2, 0) and (7/3, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundaries: 6x + 5y = 14 has intercepts (7/3, 0) and (0, 14/5); 4x + 2y = 10 has intercepts (5/2, 0) and (0, 5); 3x − 2y = 8 has intercepts (8/3, 0) and (0, −4). The origin fails 6x + 5y ≥ 14 (0 ≥ 14 false), so the region lies above that line, and below 4x + 2y = 10; the third condition 3x − 2y ≤ 8 is slack at all four corner points (at (5/2, 0), 15/2 ≤ 8). Hence the solution space is the bounded quadrilateral between the two lines in the first quadrant, with corners (0, 14/5), (0, 5), (5/2, 0), (7/3, 0).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Maximize Z(x, y) = 10x + 11y subject to 2x + 3y ≤ 8 and 6x + 3y ≤ 10.
questions.explanation: Boundary 2x + 3y = 8 gives intercepts (4, 0) and (0, 8/3); boundary 6x + 3y = 10 gives (5/3, 0) and (0, 10/3). The origin satisfies both, so the feasible region is the quadrilateral enclosed by the two lines and the axes. Subtracting the equations gives 4x = 2 ⇒ x = 1/2, and then y = (8 − 1)/3 = 7/3, so the lines meet at (1/2, 7/3). Evaluate: Z(0,0) = 0; Z(0, 8/3) = 88/3 ≈ 29.33; Z(1/2, 7/3) = 5 + 77/3 = 92/3 ≈ 30.67; Z(5/3, 0) = 50/3 ≈ 16.67. The largest value is 92/3 at (1/2, 7/3). (The printed key gives 30.6, which is this value truncated to one decimal place.)

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Maximize Z(x, y) = 30x + 36y subject to 4x + 2y ≤ 12 and 6x + 5y ≤ 20.
questions.explanation: Boundary 4x + 2y = 12 gives intercepts (3, 0) and (0, 6); boundary 6x + 5y = 20 gives (10/3, 0) and (0, 4). The origin satisfies both, so the region is the quadrilateral inside the axes. The lines meet where y = 6 − 2x and 6x + 5(6 − 2x) = 20 ⇒ 30 − 4x = 20 ⇒ x = 5/2, y = 1. Evaluate: Z(0,0) = 0; Z(0,4) = 144; Z(5/2,1) = 75 + 36 = 111; Z(3,0) = 90. Hence the maximum is 144 at (0, 4).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Maximize Z(x, y) = 41x + 38y subject to 4x + 5y ≤ 26, 8x + 5y ≤ 22 and 5x + 2y ≤ 10.
questions.explanation: Intercepts: 4x + 5y = 26 → (13/2, 0), (0, 26/5); 8x + 5y = 22 → (11/4, 0), (0, 22/5); 5x + 2y = 10 → (2, 0), (0, 5). The first constraint is not binding: every corner point determined by the other two satisfies it with slack. The binding boundaries are 8x + 5y = 22 and 5x + 2y = 10; they meet where 16x + 10y = 44 and 25x + 10y = 50, giving 9x = 6 ⇒ x = 2/3 and y = (22 − 16/3)/5 = 10/3. Evaluate: Z(0,0) = 0; Z(0, 22/5) = 38 × 22/5 = 167.2; Z(2/3, 10/3) = 82/3 + 380/3 = 154; Z(2, 0) = 82. Maximum 167.2 at (0, 22/5).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Maximize Z = 4x + y subject to x + y ≤ 50, 3x + y ≤ 90 and x − y ≤ 40.
questions.explanation: Intercepts: x + y = 50 → (50, 0), (0, 50); 3x + y = 90 → (30, 0), (0, 90); x − y = 40 → (40, 0), (0, −40). The origin satisfies all three, so the feasible region is in the first quadrant. The binding lines are x + y = 50 and 3x + y = 90, which meet where 2x = 40 ⇒ x = 20, y = 30. The line x − y = 40 is slack at (20, 30) (−10 ≤ 40) and at (30, 0) (30 ≤ 40). Evaluate: Z(0,0) = 0; Z(0,50) = 50; Z(20,30) = 110; Z(30,0) = 120. Maximum 120 at (30, 0).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Minimize Z = 200x + 500y subject to x + 2y ≥ 10 and 3x + 4y ≤ 24.
questions.answer: Minimum Z = 2300 at (x, y) = (4, 3); corner points (0, 5), (0, 6), (4, 3).
questions.explanation: Intercepts: x + 2y = 10 → (10, 0), (0, 5); 3x + 4y = 24 → (8, 0), (0, 6). The origin fails x + 2y ≥ 10, so the region is above that line and below 3x + 4y = 24 in the first quadrant. The lines meet where 2x + 4y = 20 and 3x + 4y = 24 ⇒ x = 4, y = 3. The feasible region is the triangle (0, 5), (0, 6), (4, 3). Evaluate: Z(0,5) = 2500; Z(0,6) = 3000; Z(4,3) = 800 + 1500 = 2300. Minimum 2300 at (4, 3).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Minimize Z = 3x + 2y subject to 2x + y ≥ 6 and x + y ≥ 4.
questions.answer: Minimum Z = 10 at (x, y) = (2, 2); corner points (0, 6), (2, 2), (4, 0).
questions.explanation: Intercepts: 2x + y = 6 → (3, 0), (0, 6); x + y = 4 → (4, 0), (0, 4). The origin fails both inequalities, so the region is above both lines in the first quadrant. The lines meet where (2x + y) − (x + y) = 6 − 4 ⇒ x = 2, y = 2. The feasible region is the unbounded region above the broken line through (0, 6), (2, 2), (4, 0). Evaluate: Z(0,6) = 12; Z(2,2) = 6 + 4 = 10; Z(4,0) = 12. Minimum 10 at (2, 2).

questions.question: Solve the linear programming problem by the graphical method when x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0: Minimize Z = 0.12x + 0.15y subject to x + y ≥ 5, 2x + y ≥ 6 and x + 3y ≥ 9.
questions.explanation: Intercepts: x + y = 5 → (5, 0), (0, 5); 2x + y = 6 → (3, 0), (0, 6); x + 3y = 9 → (9, 0), (0, 3). The origin fails all three, so the region is above all three lines in the first quadrant. Its corners are the intersections: 2x + y = 6 with x + y = 5 gives (1, 4); x + y = 5 with x + 3y = 9 gives (3, 2); the y-intercept (0, 6) and the x-intercept (9, 0) of the outer lines complete the boundary. Evaluate: Z(0,6) = 0.90; Z(1,4) = 0.12 + 0.60 = 0.72; Z(3,2) = 0.36 + 0.30 = 0.66; Z(9,0) = 1.08. Minimum 0.66 at (3, 2).

questions.question: A landlord has 50 hectares of land to grow two crops X and Y with profits per hectare estimated as Rs 10,500 and Rs 9,000 respectively. To control weeds, a liquid herbicide of no more than 800 litres is to be used for crops X and Y at rates of 20 litres and 10 litres per hectare. How much land should be allocated to each crop so as to maximize the total profit?
questions.answer: 30 hectares to crop X and 20 hectares to crop Y; maximum total profit = Rs 495,000.
questions.explanation: Let x = hectares under crop X and y = hectares under crop Y. Constraints: x + y ≤ 50 (land); 20x + 10y ≤ 800, i.e. 2x + y ≤ 80 (herbicide); x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Objective: maximize P = 10,500x + 9,000y. Boundaries: x + y = 50 passes through (50, 0), (0, 50); 2x + y = 80 passes through (40, 0), (0, 80). They meet where x + y = 50 and 2x + y = 80 ⇒ x = 30, y = 20. Vertices of the feasible quadrilateral: (0, 0), (40, 0), (30, 20), (0, 50). Profits: P(0,0) = 0; P(40,0) = 420,000; P(30,20) = 315,000 + 180,000 = 495,000; P(0,50) = 450,000. Maximum Rs 495,000 at (30, 20).

questions.question: A toy factory manufactures two types of toys A and B and sells them for Rs 25 and Rs 20 respectively. The toys A and B respectively require 20 units and 12 units daily out of 2000 available resource units. Both require a production time of 5 minutes and total working hours are 9 per day. What should be the quantity for each of the toys to maximize the selling amount?
questions.answer: 88 toys of type A and 20 toys of type B per day; maximum selling amount = Rs 2600.
questions.explanation: Let x = number of toys A and y = number of toys B produced daily. Constraints: 20x + 12y ≤ 2000 (resource units); 5x + 5y ≤ 540 (9 hours = 540 minutes); x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Objective: maximize S = 25x + 20y. Boundaries: 20x + 12y = 2000 passes through (100, 0) and (0, 500/3); 5x + 5y = 540, i.e. x + y = 108, passes through (108, 0) and (0, 108). They meet where y = 108 − x and 20x + 12(108 − x) = 2000 ⇒ 8x + 1296 = 2000 ⇒ x = 88, y = 20. Vertices: (0, 0), (100, 0), (88, 20), (0, 108). Selling amounts: 0; 2500; 25(88) + 20(20) = 2200 + 400 = 2600; 2160. Maximum Rs 2600 at 88 toys A and 20 toys B.

questions.question: At a university, Professor Abdul Sattar wishes to employ two people, Farhan and Sarfaraz, to grade papers. Farhan is a graduate student and can grade 20 papers per hour; Farhan earns $15 per hour for grading papers. Sarfaraz is a post-doctoral associate and can grade 30 papers per hour; Sarfaraz earns $25 per hour for grading papers. Each must be employed at least one hour a week to justify their employment. If Prof. Abdul Sattar has at least 110 papers to be graded each week, how many hours per week should he employ each person to minimize the cost?
questions.answer: Employ Farhan for 4 hours and Sarfaraz for 1 hour per week; minimum cost = $85 per week.
questions.explanation: Let x = hours per week for Farhan and y = hours per week for Sarfaraz. Constraints: x ≥ 1, y ≥ 1 (each employed at least one hour); 20x + 30y ≥ 110 (papers graded). Objective: minimize C = 15x + 25y. The line 20x + 30y = 110, i.e. 2x + 3y = 11, cuts x = 1 at y = 3 and y = 1 at x = 4, so the feasible corner points are (1, 3) and (4, 1) (the region is unbounded above and to the right). Costs: C(1,3) = 15 + 75 = 90; C(4,1) = 60 + 25 = 85. Along the constraint line C = 15x + 25(110 − 20x)/30 = 91.67 − 1.67x decreases as x increases, so the least cost is $85 at (4, 1): Farhan 4 hours and Sarfaraz 1 hour. Check: 20(4) + 30(1) = 110 papers.

questions.question: If 2x − 5 ≥ 3 then its solution set is ________, where x ∈ ℤ.
questions.explanation: 2x − 5 ≥ 3 ⇒ 2x ≥ 8 ⇒ x ≥ 4. Since x is an integer, the solution set is {4, 5, 6, ...}.

questions.question: If 4x − 3y = 8 is the corresponding equation of an inequality 4x − 3y ≤ 8 then its x-intercept is ________.
questions.explanation: The x-intercept is found by putting y = 0: 4x − 3(0) = 8 ⇒ 4x = 8 ⇒ x = 2. So the line cuts the x-axis at (2, 0).

questions.question: {x | x ∈ ℝ ∧ x > 5} = ________.
questions.explanation: The set of all real numbers strictly greater than 5 is the open interval (5, ∞); the endpoint 5 is not included because the inequality is strict.

questions.question: Linear Programming (LP) is used to obtain ________ solution.
questions.explanation: An LP problem seeks the best (maximum or minimum) value of a linear objective function subject to linear constraints; that best feasible solution is called the optimal solution.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Feasible  b) Trivial  c) Optimal  d) Infeasible

questions.question: Solution space of the linear inequality 2x + 3y ≤ 6, ∀ x, y ∈ ℝ includes ________.
questions.answer: (b) All points on and below the line
questions.explanation: 2x + 3y ≤ 6 can be written y ≤ (6 − 2x)/3, so the solution space is the half-plane bounded by the line 2x + 3y = 6 on and below it; the boundary is included because of ≤.

options.text: All points on and below the line
All points on and above the line

questions.optionsRaw: a) All points above the line  b) All points on and below the line  c) All points below the line  d) All points on and above the line
questions.correctAnswer: (b) All points on and below the line

questions.question: If f(x, y) = 5x + 4y is an objective function and the corner points of the feasible region are (5, 4), (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6) then the function is maximum at:
questions.explanation: Evaluate f at each corner: f(5,4) = 25 + 16 = 41; f(0,0) = 0; f(4,0) = 20; f(0,6) = 24. The largest value is 41, attained at (5, 4).

questions.question: ________ are the entities whose values are to be determined from the solution of the LP problem.
questions.explanation: The unknown quantities of an LP problem (usually x, y, z, ...) whose values the solution must determine are called decision variables; they are required to be non-negative.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Objective function  b) Decision Variables  c) Constraints  d) Opportunity cost

questions.question: ________ specifies the objective or goal of solving the LP problem.
questions.explanation: The objective function Z = ax + by expresses the aim of the problem (for example profit to be maximized or cost to be minimized).
questions.optionsRaw: a) Objective function  b) Decision Variables  c) Constraints  d) Opportunity cost

questions.question: ________ are the restrictions or limitations imposed on the LP problem:
questions.explanation: The linear inequalities or equations that restrict the decision variables (including the non-negativity restrictions x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0) are the problem constraints.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Variables  b) Costs  c) Profits  d) Constraints

questions.question: The region of solution in LP problem is called ________.
questions.explanation: The common region determined by all the constraints, including the non-negative restrictions, is called the feasible region (or solution space).
questions.optionsRaw: a) Infeasible region  b) Unbounded region  c) Infinite region  d) Feasible region

questions.question: In case of an '________' constraint, the feasible region is a straight line.
questions.explanation: For an equality constraint ax + by = c the set of feasible points lies exactly on the line, so the feasible region reduces to (a part of) a straight line rather than a half-plane.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Less than or equal to  b) Greater than or equal to  c) Mixed  d) Equal to

questions.question: ax + b ≤ 0, a ≠ 0, a, b ∈ ℝ, is called ________.
questions.explanation: The expression involves the variable x only to the first power and the relation is an inequality (≤), so it is a linear inequality in one variable.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Non-linear inequality  b) Linear inequality  c) Linear equality  d) Complex inequality

questions.question: A point of a solution region where two of its boundary lines intersect, is called ________.
questions.explanation: A vertex of the feasible region, formed by the intersection of two boundary lines, is called a corner point; the optimum of an LP problem occurs at a corner point.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Middle point  b) Origin  c) Corner point  d) Feasible point

questions.question: The solution region of an inequality restricted to the first quadrant is called ________ region.
questions.explanation: Points of the first quadrant (x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0) that satisfy all the constraints form the feasible region of the problem.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Combined  b) Unbounded  c) Infeasible  d) Feasible

questions.question: A function which is to be maximized or minimized is called ________.
questions.explanation: In an LP problem the linear function Z = ax + by whose value is to be maximized or minimized is called the objective function.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Linear function  b) Equal function  c) Objective function  d) Non linear function

questions.question: The feasible solution which maximizes or minimizes the objective function is called the ________.
questions.explanation: The feasible solution giving the largest objective value (maximization) or the smallest (minimization) is the optimal solution.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Optimal solution  b) Corner solution  c) Initial solution  d) Complex solution

questions.question: Draw the graph of the system of linear inequalities 2x + 3y ≥ 10, 3x + 2y ≥ 12, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 and find the feasible region.
questions.answer: Feasible region: the unbounded region above both lines in the first quadrant, with corner points (0, 6), (16/5, 6/5) and (5, 0).
questions.explanation: Boundary 2x + 3y = 10 cuts the axes at (5, 0) and (0, 10/3); boundary 3x + 2y = 12 cuts them at (4, 0) and (0, 6). The origin fails both inequalities, so shade the half-plane above each line, restricted to the first quadrant. The lines meet where 2x + 3y = 10 and 3x + 2y = 12: multiplying the first by 3 and the second by 2 gives 6x + 9y = 30 and 6x + 4y = 24, so 5y = 6 ⇒ y = 6/5 and x = (10 − 18/5)/2 = 16/5. The feasible region is the unbounded region above the broken line through (0, 6), (16/5, 6/5), (5, 0).

questions.question: Find the feasible region graphically subject to the constraints 4x + y ≥ 9, 2x + 3y ≤ 14, x − y ≤ 5, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, and also find its corner points.
questions.answer: Corner points of the feasible region: (9/4, 0), (13/10, 19/5), (29/5, 4/5) and (5, 0); the region is bounded.
questions.explanation: Boundaries: 4x + y = 9 through (9/4, 0), (0, 9); 2x + 3y = 14 through (7, 0), (0, 14/3); x − y = 5 through (5, 0), (0, −5). The origin fails 4x + y ≥ 9, so the region is above 4x + y = 9, below 2x + 3y = 14, and on the side of x − y = 5 containing the origin (x − y ≤ 5). Intersections: 4x + y = 9 with y = 0 gives (9/4, 0); 4x + y = 9 with 2x + 3y = 14 gives x = 13/10, y = 19/5; 2x + 3y = 14 with x − y = 5 gives x = 29/5, y = 4/5; x − y = 5 with y = 0 gives (5, 0). The region is the bounded quadrilateral with these four corner points.

questions.question: Find the maximum and minimum values of the function f(x, y) = 4x − 3y subject to the constraints 2x + 3y ≥ 5, 3x + 2y ≤ 12, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.
questions.answer: Maximum f = 16 at (4, 0); minimum f = −18 at (0, 6); corner points (0, 5/3), (0, 6), (4, 0), (5/2, 0).
questions.explanation: Intercepts: 2x + 3y = 5 → (5/2, 0), (0, 5/3); 3x + 2y = 12 → (4, 0), (0, 6). The origin fails 2x + 3y ≥ 5, so the region is above this line, below 3x + 2y = 12 and in the first quadrant; its corners are (0, 5/3), (0, 6), (4, 0), (5/2, 0). Values: f(0, 5/3) = −5; f(0, 6) = −18; f(4, 0) = 16; f(5/2, 0) = 10. Hence the maximum is 16 at (4, 0) and the minimum is −18 at (0, 6). (The printed key states the minimum as 10 at (5/2, 0), but f(0, 6) = −18 is smaller, so that key entry is incorrect.)

questions.question: A dealer wishes to purchase some fans and sewing machines. He has only ¥ 5760 to invest and space of at most 20 items. The costs of a fan and a sewing machine are ¥ 360 and ¥ 240 respectively. He wants profit on a fan and a sewing machine ¥ 22 and ¥ 18 respectively. Assuming that he can sell all the items that he can buy, how should he invest his money in order to maximize his profit?
questions.answer: Buy 8 fans and 12 sewing machines; maximum profit = ¥ 392 (investment = ¥ 5760).
questions.explanation: Let x = number of fans and y = number of sewing machines. Constraints: 360x + 240y ≤ 5760, i.e. 3x + 2y ≤ 48 (money); x + y ≤ 20 (space); x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Objective: maximize P = 22x + 18y. Boundaries: 3x + 2y = 48 passes through (16, 0), (0, 24); x + y = 20 passes through (20, 0), (0, 20). They meet where y = 20 − x and 3x + 2(20 − x) = 48 ⇒ x + 40 = 48 ⇒ x = 8, y = 12. Vertices: (0, 0), (16, 0), (8, 12), (0, 20). Profits: 0; 22(16) = 352; 22(8) + 18(12) = 176 + 216 = 392; 18(20) = 360. Maximum ¥ 392 at (8, 12): 8 fans and 12 sewing machines, using 360(8) + 240(12) = 2880 + 2880 = ¥ 5760 and 20 items.

questions.question: Prove that: cos(360° + θ) = cos θ.
questions.explanation:
Use cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B with A = 360°, B = θ:
cos(360° + θ) = cos 360° cos θ − sin 360° sin θ = (1)cos θ − (0)sin θ = cos θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: sin(180° + θ) = −sin θ.
questions.explanation:
Use sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B with A = 180°, B = θ:
sin(180° + θ) = sin 180° cos θ + cos 180° sin θ = (0)cos θ + (−1)sin θ = −sin θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ.
questions.explanation:
Use tan(A − B) = (tan A − tan B)/(1 + tan A tan B) with A = 180°, B = θ:
tan(180° − θ) = (tan 180° − tan θ)/(1 + tan 180° tan θ) = (0 − tan θ)/(1 + 0) = −tan θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: sin(270° − θ) = −cos θ.
questions.explanation:
Use sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B with A = 270°, B = θ:
sin(270° − θ) = sin 270° cos θ − cos 270° sin θ = (−1)cos θ − (0)sin θ = −cos θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cot(270° + θ) = −tan θ.
questions.explanation:
Write cot as cos/sin and expand both:
cos(270° + θ) = cos 270° cos θ − sin 270° sin θ = 0 − (−1)sin θ = sin θ,
sin(270° + θ) = sin 270° cos θ + cos 270° sin θ = −cos θ + 0 = −cos θ.
Hence cot(270° + θ) = sin θ/(−cos θ) = −tan θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cot(270° − θ) = tan θ.
questions.explanation:
cos(270° − θ) = cos 270° cos θ + sin 270° sin θ = 0 + (−1)sin θ = −sin θ,
sin(270° − θ) = sin 270° cos θ − cos 270° sin θ = −cos θ − 0 = −cos θ.
Hence cot(270° − θ) = (−sin θ)/(−cos θ) = tan θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cosec(360° − θ) = −cosec θ.
questions.explanation:
sin(360° − θ) = sin 360° cos θ − cos 360° sin θ = 0 − (1)sin θ = −sin θ.
Therefore cosec(360° − θ) = 1/sin(360° − θ) = 1/(−sin θ) = −cosec θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: sec(360° − θ) = sec θ.
questions.explanation:
cos(360° − θ) = cos 360° cos θ + sin 360° sin θ = (1)cos θ + 0 = cos θ.
Therefore sec(360° − θ) = 1/cos(360° − θ) = 1/cos θ = sec θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Evaluate: sin 150° cos 300° + sin 300° cos 150°.
questions.explanation:
This is the expansion of sin(A + B) with A = 150°, B = 300°:
sin 150° cos 300° + sin 300° cos 150° = sin(150° + 300°) = sin 450° = sin(450° − 360°) = sin 90° = 1.

questions.question: Evaluate: cos 19° cos 11° − sin 19° sin 11°.
questions.explanation:
This is the expansion of cos(A + B) with A = 19°, B = 11°:
cos 19° cos 11° − sin 19° sin 11° = cos(19° + 11°) = cos 30° = √3/2.

Prove that: [sin(α + β) + sin(α − β)]/[cos(α + β) + cos(α − β)] = tan α.
questions.explanation:
Expand both sums:
sin(α + β) + sin(α − β) = (sin α cos β + cos α sin β) + (sin α cos β − cos α sin β) = 2 sin α cos β,
cos(α + β) + cos(α − β) = (cos α cos β − sin α sin β) + (cos α cos β + sin α sin β) = 2 cos α cos β.
Therefore L.H.S. = (2 sin α cos β)/(2 cos α cos β) = sin α/cos α = tan α = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: [cos(α + β) + cos(α − β)]/[sin(α + β) + sin(α − β)] = cot α.
questions.explanation:
From the expansions, the numerator is 2 cos α cos β and the denominator is 2 sin α cos β:
cos(α + β) + cos(α − β) = 2 cos α cos β,
sin(α + β) + sin(α − β) = 2 sin α cos β.
Hence L.H.S. = (2 cos α cos β)/(2 sin α cos β) = cos α/sin α = cot α = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: sin(α + β) sin(α − β) = sin²α − sin²β.
questions.explanation:
L.H.S. = (sin α cos β + cos α sin β)(sin α cos β − cos α sin β)
= sin²α cos²β − cos²α sin²β
= sin²α(1 − sin²β) − (1 − sin²α)sin²β
= sin²α − sin²α sin²β − sin²β + sin²α sin²β = sin²α − sin²β = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cos(α + β) cos(α − β) = cos²α − sin²β.
questions.explanation:
L.H.S. = (cos α cos β − sin α sin β)(cos α cos β + sin α sin β)
= cos²α cos²β − sin²α sin²β
= cos²α(1 − sin²β) − (1 − cos²α)sin²β
= cos²α − cos²α sin²β − sin²β + cos²α sin²β = cos²α − sin²β = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cos(α + β) + cos(α − β) = 2 cos α cos β.
questions.explanation:
cos(α + β) = cos α cos β − sin α sin β and cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β.
Adding the two equations gives cos(α + β) + cos(α − β) = 2 cos α cos β = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove that: cos α cos(β − α) − sin α sin(β − α) = cos β.
questions.explanation:
The left side is the expansion of cos(α + (β − α)):
cos α cos(β − α) − sin α sin(β − α) = cos(α + β − α) = cos β = R.H.S.
Equivalently, expand cos(β − α) and sin(β − α): cos²α cos β + cos α sin α sin β − sin α sin β cos α + sin²α cos β = (cos²α + sin²α)cos β = cos β.

questions.question: If sin α = 12/13 and sin β = 3/5, where 0 < α < π/2 and 0 < β < π/2, then find cos(α + β).

questions.question: If sin α = 12/13 and sin β = 3/5, where 0 < α < π/2 and 0 < β < π/2, then find cot(α − β).

cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = 20/65 + 36/65 = 56/65 and sin(α − β) = sin α cos β − cos α sin β = 48/65 − 15/65 = 33/65.
cot(α − β) = cos(α − β)/sin(α − β) = (56/65)/(33/65) = 56/33.

questions.explanation:
From 8(iii) and 8(iv), sin(α − β) = 33/65 and cos(α − β) = 56/65.
tan(α − β) = sin(α − β)/cos(α − β) = (33/65)/(56/65) = 33/56.

questions.question: If sin α = 12/13 and sin β = 3/5, where 0 < α < π/2 and 0 < β < π/2, also find the quadrants in which the angles (α + β) and (α − β) lie.
questions.answer: α + β lies in the 2nd quadrant; α − β lies in the 1st quadrant.
questions.explanation:
sin(α + β) = 63/65 > 0 while cos(α + β) = −16/65 < 0, so α + β is in the 2nd quadrant.
sin(α − β) = 33/65 > 0 and cos(α − β) = 56/65 > 0, so α − β is in the 1st quadrant.

questions.question: Generate all allied angles if θ = 60°.
Generate all allied angles if θ = 50°.
Show that: sin(90° − θ)/cosec(90° − θ) + cos(90° − θ)/sec(90° − θ) = 1.
questions.explanation:
Using co-ratios: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cosec(90° − θ) = sec θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.
L.H.S. = cos θ/sec θ + sin θ/cosec θ = cos θ · cos θ + sin θ · sin θ = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Show that: sin²2° + sin²3° + sin²87° + sin²88° = 2.
questions.explanation:
Since sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, sin 87° = cos 3° and sin 88° = cos 2°.
L.H.S. = (sin²2° + cos²2°) + (sin²3° + cos²3°) = 1 + 1 = 2 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Evaluate without using calculator: sin 675°.
Evaluate without using calculator: tan(25π/6).
questions.explanation:
25π/6 = 4π + π/6, and tangent has period π:
tan(25π/6) = tan(4π + π/6) = tan(π/6) = 1/√3.

questions.question: Evaluate without using calculator: cosec(2130°).
Evaluate without using calculator: sec 55°/cosec 35° + sin 48°/cos 42°.
questions.explanation:
sec 55° = cosec(90° − 55°) = cosec 35°, so sec 55°/cosec 35° = 1.
sin 48° = cos(90° − 48°) = cos 42°, so sin 48°/cos 42° = 1.
Therefore the expression equals 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.question: Evaluate without using calculator: 2 sin 56°/cos 34° − cot 37°/tan 53° − √2 sin 45°.
questions.explanation:
sin 56° = cos 34°, so 2 sin 56°/cos 34° = 2.
cot 37° = tan(90° − 37°) = tan 53°, so cot 37°/tan 53° = 1.
√2 sin 45° = √2 · (1/√2) = 1.
Hence the expression = 2 − 1 − 1 = 0.

questions.question: Evaluate without using calculator: cos 1° + cos 2° + cos 3° + … + cos 180°.
questions.explanation:
Pair each term with its supplement: cos θ + cos(180° − θ) = cos θ − cos θ = 0.
The pairs (1°, 179°), (2°, 178°), …, (89°, 91°) all cancel, leaving cos 90° + cos 180° = 0 + (−1) = −1.
Printed key gives (vi) 1; the correct value is −1 (the key has interchanged the answers of (vi) and (vii)).

questions.question: Evaluate without using calculator: tan 1° · tan 2° · tan 3° · … · tan 89°.
questions.explanation:
For each θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, so tan θ · tan(90° − θ) = tan θ · cot θ = 1.
Pairing 1° with 89°, 2° with 88°, …, 44° with 46° gives 44 factors equal to 1, and the middle factor is tan 45° = 1.
Hence the product is 1. Printed key gives (vii) −1; the correct value is 1 (the key has interchanged the answers of (vi) and (vii)).

questions.question: Show that: cos(45° − θ) = (1/√2)(cos θ + sin θ).
questions.explanation:
cos(45° − θ) = cos 45° cos θ + sin 45° sin θ
= (1/√2)cos θ + (1/√2)sin θ = (1/√2)(cos θ + sin θ) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Show that: tan(45° + θ) tan(45° − θ) = 1.
questions.explanation:
tan(45° + θ) = (1 + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ) and tan(45° − θ) = (1 − tan θ)/(1 + tan θ).
Their product is [(1 + tan θ)(1 − tan θ)]/[(1 − tan θ)(1 + tan θ)] = 1 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Express 15 sin θ + 8 cos θ in the form r sin(θ + φ), where θ and φ are in the first quadrant.
questions.answer: 17 sin(θ + φ), where cos φ = 15/17 and sin φ = 8/17.
questions.explanation:
Write 15 = r cos φ and 8 = r sin φ. Squaring and adding: r² = 15² + 8² = 225 + 64 = 289, so r = 17.
Then cos φ = 15/17 and sin φ = 8/17 (φ acute).
15 sin θ + 8 cos θ = r sin θ cos φ + r cos θ sin φ = r sin(θ + φ) = 17 sin(θ + φ).

questions.question: Express (√3/2) sin θ + (1/2) cos θ in the form r sin(θ + φ), where θ and φ are in the first quadrant.
questions.answer: sin(θ + φ), where cos φ = √3/2 and sin φ = 1/2 (φ = 30°).
questions.explanation:
Here a = √3/2 and b = 1/2, so r = √(3/4 + 1/4) = 1.
cos φ = √3/2 and sin φ = 1/2, hence φ = 30°.
(√3/2) sin θ + (1/2) cos θ = sin θ cos 30° + cos θ sin 30° = sin(θ + 30°) = sin(θ + φ).

questions.question: Express sin θ + cos θ in the form r sin(θ + φ), where θ and φ are in the first quadrant.
questions.answer: √2 sin(θ + φ), where cos φ = 1/√2 and sin φ = 1/√2 (φ = 45°).
questions.explanation:
a = 1, b = 1, so r = √(1² + 1²) = √2; cos φ = 1/√2 and sin φ = 1/√2, giving φ = 45°.
sin θ + cos θ = √2[(1/√2)sin θ + (1/√2)cos θ] = √2 sin(θ + 45°) = √2 sin(θ + φ).

questions.question: Prove that: tan α/cot(90° − α) + cos(90° − α)/sin α = 2.
questions.explanation:
cot(90° − α) = tan α and cos(90° − α) = sin α.
L.H.S. = tan α/tan α + sin α/sin α = 1 + 1 = 2 = R.H.S.

questions.question: If A + B + C = 180°, prove that: tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A tan B tan C.
questions.explanation:
Since A + B = 180° − C, tan(A + B) = tan(180° − C) = −tan C.
But tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B). Hence
(tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B) = −tan C
⇒ tan A + tan B = −tan C + tan A tan B tan C
⇒ tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A tan B tan C = R.H.S.

questions.question: If A + B + C = 180°, prove that: cos((B + C)/2) = sin(A/2).
If A + B + C = 180°, prove that: tan(A/2) tan(B/2) + tan(B/2) tan(C/2) + tan(C/2) tan(A/2) = 1.
questions.explanation:
A/2 + B/2 = 90° − C/2, so tan(A/2 + B/2) = tan(90° − C/2) = cot(C/2) = 1/tan(C/2).
Using the tangent addition formula:
[tan(A/2) + tan(B/2)]/[1 − tan(A/2)tan(B/2)] = 1/tan(C/2).
Cross-multiplying:
tan(C/2)[tan(A/2) + tan(B/2)] = 1 − tan(A/2)tan(B/2)
⇒ tan(A/2)tan(C/2) + tan(B/2)tan(C/2) + tan(A/2)tan(B/2) = 1 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: sin 2θ/sin θ − cos 2θ/cos θ = sec θ.
questions.explanation:
L.H.S. = (2 sin θ cos θ)/sin θ − (2 cos²θ − 1)/cos θ
= 2 cos θ − 2 cos θ + 1/cos θ = 1/cos θ = sec θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: sin 3α/sin α − cos 3α/cos α = 2.
questions.explanation:
Use sin 3α = 3 sin α − 4 sin³α and cos 3α = 4 cos³α − 3 cos α:
L.H.S. = (3 − 4 sin²α) − (4 cos²α − 3) = 6 − 4(sin²α + cos²α) = 6 − 4 = 2 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: sin 4θ/sin 2θ − cos 4θ/cos 2θ = sec 2θ.
questions.explanation:
sin 4θ = 2 sin 2θ cos 2θ and cos 4θ = 2 cos²2θ − 1.
L.H.S. = 2 cos 2θ − (2 cos²2θ − 1)/cos 2θ = 2 cos 2θ − 2 cos 2θ + 1/cos 2θ = sec 2θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cos 2α = (1 − tan²α)/(1 + tan²α).
questions.explanation:
Write tan α = sin α/cos α and multiply numerator and denominator by cos²α:
R.H.S. = (cos²α − sin²α)/(cos²α + sin²α) = cos 2α/1 = cos 2α = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (cos(θ/2) − sin(θ/2))² = 1 − sin θ.
questions.explanation:
L.H.S. = cos²(θ/2) + sin²(θ/2) − 2 sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2)
= 1 − sin θ = R.H.S. (using 2 sin x cos x = sin 2x with x = θ/2).

questions.question: Prove the identity: sin 2α = 2 tan α/(1 + tan²α).
questions.explanation:
R.H.S. = [2(sin α/cos α)]/[1 + sin²α/cos²α]
= (2 sin α cos α)/(cos²α + sin²α) = 2 sin α cos α = sin 2α = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cos 2θ = (cot²θ − 1)/(cot²θ + 1).
questions.explanation:
R.H.S. = (cos²θ/sin²θ − 1)/(cos²θ/sin²θ + 1)
= (cos²θ − sin²θ)/(cos²θ + sin²θ) = cos 2θ = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: sin 4θ = 4 sin θ cos θ cos 2θ.
questions.explanation: R.H.S. = 2(2 sin θ cos θ)cos 2θ = 2 sin 2θ cos 2θ = sin 4θ = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cos 4θ = 8 cos⁴θ − 8 cos²θ + 1.
questions.explanation:
cos 4θ = 2 cos²2θ − 1 = 2(2 cos²θ − 1)² − 1
= 2(4 cos⁴θ − 4 cos²θ + 1) − 1 = 8 cos⁴θ − 8 cos²θ + 1 = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: tan(α/2) = cosec α − cot α.
questions.explanation:
R.H.S. = 1/sin α − cos α/sin α = (1 − cos α)/sin α.
Now tan(α/2) = sin α/(1 + cos α); multiplying numerator and denominator by (1 − cos α) gives
sin α(1 − cos α)/(1 − cos²α) = (1 − cos α)/sin α.
Hence tan(α/2) = cosec α − cot α = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cosec²(θ/2) = 2 sec θ/(sec θ − 1).
questions.explanation:
L.H.S. = 1/sin²(θ/2) = 2/(1 − cos θ).
Multiply numerator and denominator by sec θ:
2/(1 − cos θ) = 2 sec θ/(sec θ − 1) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin θ + sin 2θ)/(1 + cos θ + cos 2θ) = tan θ.
questions.explanation:
Numerator = sin θ + 2 sin θ cos θ = sin θ(1 + 2 cos θ).
Denominator = 1 + cos θ + (2 cos²θ − 1) = cos θ(1 + 2 cos θ).
L.H.S. = sin θ(1 + 2 cos θ)/[cos θ(1 + 2 cos θ)] = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: tan 4θ = 4 tan θ(1 − tan²θ)/(tan⁴θ − 6 tan²θ + 1).
questions.explanation:
Let t = tan θ. tan 2θ = 2t/(1 − t²), so
tan 4θ = 2 tan 2θ/(1 − tan²2θ) = [2(2t/(1 − t²))]/[1 − 4t²/(1 − t²)²]
= [4t/(1 − t²)] · [(1 − t²)²/((1 − t²)² − 4t²)]
= 4t(1 − t²)/(1 − 2t² + t⁴ − 4t²) = 4 tan θ(1 − tan²θ)/(tan⁴θ − 6 tan²θ + 1) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: sec θ = (tan(θ/2) + cot(θ/2))/(cot(θ/2) − tan(θ/2)).
questions.explanation:
Let x = tan(θ/2). Then
R.H.S. = (x + 1/x)/(1/x − x) = (x² + 1)/(1 − x²).
But cos θ = (1 − x²)/(1 + x²), so R.H.S. = 1/cos θ = sec θ = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: cot 2θ = (cot θ − tan θ)/2.
questions.explanation:
R.H.S. = [(cos θ/sin θ) − (sin θ/cos θ)]/2
= [(cos²θ − sin²θ)/(sin θ cos θ)]/2 = cos 2θ/(2 sin θ cos θ)
= cos 2θ/sin 2θ = cot 2θ = L.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: tan²(θ/2) = (tan θ − sin θ)/(tan θ + sin θ).
questions.explanation:
R.H.S. = [sin θ(1/cos θ − 1)]/[sin θ(1/cos θ + 1)]
= [(1 − cos θ)/cos θ]/[(1 + cos θ)/cos θ] = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ)
= tan²(θ/2) = L.H.S.

questions.question: Evaluate: tan 22.5°.
Evaluate: cos 15°.
If cos θ = −4/5 and π/2 < θ < π, find sin(θ/2).
questions.explanation:
θ is in the second quadrant, so sin θ = +3/5. Since π/2 < θ < π, we have π/4 < θ/2 < π/2, so sin(θ/2) > 0.
sin(θ/2) = √((1 − cos θ)/2) = √((1 + 4/5)/2) = √(9/10) = 3/√10.

questions.question: If cos θ = −4/5 and π/2 < θ < π, find cos(θ/2).
questions.explanation: cos(θ/2) = √((1 + cos θ)/2) = √((1 − 4/5)/2) = √(1/10) = 1/√10 (positive because θ/2 is in the first quadrant).

questions.question: If cos θ = −4/5 and π/2 < θ < π, find tan(θ/2).
If cos θ = −4/5 and π/2 < θ < π, find sin 2θ.

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: 2 sin 6θ cos 3θ.
questions.explanation:
Use 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B) with A = 6θ, B = 3θ:
2 sin 6θ cos 3θ = sin(6θ + 3θ) + sin(6θ − 3θ) = sin 9θ + sin 3θ.

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: cos 3θ sin 6θ.
questions.explanation:
Use 2 cos A sin B = sin(A + B) − sin(A − B) with A = 3θ, B = 6θ:
cos 3θ sin 6θ = ½[sin(3θ + 6θ) − sin(3θ − 6θ)] = ½[sin 9θ − sin(−3θ)] = ½(sin 9θ + sin 3θ).

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: 2 sin(α − β) cos(α + β).
questions.explanation:
Use 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B) with A = α − β, B = α + β:
2 sin(α − β)cos(α + β) = sin(2α) + sin(−2β) = sin 2α − sin 2β.

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: −2 sin((α + β)/2) sin((α − β)/2).
questions.explanation:
Use −2 sin A sin B = cos(A + B) − cos(A − B) with A = (α + β)/2, B = (α − β)/2:
−2 sin((α + β)/2)sin((α − β)/2) = cos α − cos β.

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: sin(θ + 45°) sin(θ − 45°).
questions.explanation:
Use sin A sin B = ½[cos(A − B) − cos(A + B)] with A = θ + 45°, B = θ − 45°:
sin(θ + 45°)sin(θ − 45°) = ½[cos 90° − cos 2θ] = ½[0 − cos 2θ] = −½ cos 2θ.

questions.question: Express the following product as a sum or difference: 2 cos(2θ + 60°) cos(2θ − 60°).
questions.explanation:
Use 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A − B) with A = 2θ + 60°, B = 2θ − 60°:
2 cos(2θ + 60°)cos(2θ − 60°) = cos 4θ + cos 120° = cos 4θ − ½.

questions.question: Express the following sum or difference as a product: sin 2α − sin 2β.
questions.explanation:
Use sin u − sin v = 2 cos((u + v)/2) sin((u − v)/2) with u = 2α, v = 2β:
sin 2α − sin 2β = 2 cos(α + β) sin(α − β).

questions.question: Express the following sum or difference as a product: cos(5θ/2) + cos(3θ/2).
questions.explanation:
Use cos u + cos v = 2 cos((u + v)/2) cos((u − v)/2) with u = 5θ/2, v = 3θ/2:
cos(5θ/2) + cos(3θ/2) = 2 cos(2θ) cos(θ/2).

questions.question: Express the following sum or difference as a product: cos 25° + cos 65°.
Express the following sum or difference as a product: cos(θ + 30°) − cos(θ − 30°).
questions.explanation:
Use cos u − cos v = −2 sin((u + v)/2) sin((u − v)/2) with u = θ + 30°, v = θ − 30°:
= −2 sin θ sin 30° = −2 sin θ (1/2) = −sin θ.

questions.question: Express the following sum or difference as a product: sin(π/2) − sin(π/4).
Express the following sum or difference as a product: sin 2(θ + 40°) + sin 2(θ − 40°).
questions.explanation:
Use sin u + sin v = 2 sin((u + v)/2) cos((u − v)/2) with u = 2(θ + 40°), v = 2(θ − 40°):
= 2 sin(2θ) cos 80° = 2 sin 2θ cos 80°.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin α − sin β)/(cos α + cos β) = tan((α − β)/2).
questions.explanation:
sin α − sin β = 2 cos((α + β)/2) sin((α − β)/2) and cos α + cos β = 2 cos((α + β)/2) cos((α − β)/2).
L.H.S. = [2 cos((α + β)/2) sin((α − β)/2)]/[2 cos((α + β)/2) cos((α − β)/2)]
= sin((α − β)/2)/cos((α − β)/2) = tan((α − β)/2) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin α + sin β)/(sin α − sin β) = tan((α + β)/2) cot((α − β)/2).
questions.explanation:
sin α + sin β = 2 sin((α + β)/2) cos((α − β)/2) and sin α − sin β = 2 cos((α + β)/2) sin((α − β)/2).
L.H.S. = [2 sin((α + β)/2) cos((α − β)/2)]/[2 cos((α + β)/2) sin((α − β)/2)]
= tan((α + β)/2) cot((α − β)/2) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin 6θ + sin 4θ)/(cos 6θ + cos 4θ) = tan 5θ.
questions.explanation:
sin 6θ + sin 4θ = 2 sin 5θ cos θ and cos 6θ + cos 4θ = 2 cos 5θ cos θ.
L.H.S. = (2 sin 5θ cos θ)/(2 cos 5θ cos θ) = tan 5θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin 2θ + sin 4θ + sin 6θ + sin 8θ)/(cos 2θ + cos 4θ + cos 6θ + cos 8θ) = tan 5θ.
questions.explanation:
Numerator = (sin 2θ + sin 8θ) + (sin 4θ + sin 6θ) = 2 sin 5θ cos 3θ + 2 sin 5θ cos θ
= 2 sin 5θ(cos 3θ + cos θ) = 2 sin 5θ (2 cos 2θ cos θ) = 4 sin 5θ cos 2θ cos θ.
Denominator = (cos 2θ + cos 8θ) + (cos 4θ + cos 6θ) = 2 cos 5θ cos 3θ + 2 cos 5θ cos θ
= 2 cos 5θ(cos 3θ + cos θ) = 4 cos 5θ cos 2θ cos θ.
Hence L.H.S. = (4 sin 5θ cos 2θ cos θ)/(4 cos 5θ cos 2θ cos θ) = tan 5θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: (sin α + sin 2α)/(cos α − cos 2α) = cot(α/2).
questions.explanation:
Numerator = 2 sin(3α/2) cos(α/2).
Denominator = cos α − cos 2α = −2 sin(3α/2) sin(−α/2) = 2 sin(3α/2) sin(α/2).
L.H.S. = [2 sin(3α/2) cos(α/2)]/[2 sin(3α/2) sin(α/2)] = cos(α/2)/sin(α/2) = cot(α/2) = R.H.S.

questions.question: Prove the identity: [sin(θ + φ) − 2 sin θ + sin(θ − φ)]/[cos(θ + φ) − 2 cos θ + cos(θ − φ)] = tan θ.
questions.explanation:
Numerator = sin(θ + φ) + sin(θ − φ) − 2 sin θ = 2 sin θ cos φ − 2 sin θ = 2 sin θ(cos φ − 1).
Denominator = cos(θ + φ) + cos(θ − φ) − 2 cos θ = 2 cos θ cos φ − 2 cos θ = 2 cos θ(cos φ − 1).
L.H.S. = [2 sin θ(cos φ − 1)]/[2 cos θ(cos φ − 1)] = tan θ = R.H.S.

questions.question: Evaluate: sin 20° sin 40° sin 60° sin 80°.
questions.explanation:
sin 60° = √3/2, so the product is (√3/2) sin 20° sin 40° sin 80°.
sin 20° sin 40° = ½[cos 20° − cos 60°] = ½[cos 20° − ½].
Hence sin 20° sin 40° sin 80° = ½ cos 20° sin 80° − ¼ sin 80°
= ¼[sin 100° + sin 60°] − ¼ sin 80° = ¼[sin 80° + √3/2] − ¼ sin 80° = √3/8.
Therefore the required product = (√3/2)(√3/8) = 3/16.

questions.question: Evaluate: cos 20° cos 40° cos 60° cos 80°.
questions.explanation:
cos 60° = ½, so the product is ½ cos 20° cos 40° cos 80°.
cos 20° cos 40° = ½[cos 60° + cos 20°] = ½[½ + cos 20°].
Hence cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° = ¼ cos 80° + ½ cos 20° cos 80°
= ¼ cos 80° + ¼[cos 100° + cos 60°] = ¼ cos 80° + ¼[−cos 80° + ½] = 1/8.
Therefore the required product = ½ · 1/8 = 1/16.

questions.question: Show that: (cos 8° − sin 8°)/(cos 8° + sin 8°) = tan 37°.
questions.explanation:
Divide numerator and denominator by cos 8°:
L.H.S. = (1 − tan 8°)/(1 + tan 8°) = tan(45° − 8°) = tan 37° = R.H.S.

questions.question: Show that: (cos 11° + sin 11°)/(cos 11° − sin 11°) = tan 56°.
questions.explanation:
Divide numerator and denominator by cos 11°:
L.H.S. = (1 + tan 11°)/(1 − tan 11°) = tan(45° + 11°) = tan 56° = R.H.S.

questions.question: Show that: sin 50° − sin 70° + sin 10° = 0.
questions.explanation:
sin 50° − sin 70° = 2 cos(60°) sin(−10°) = 2(1/2)(−sin 10°) = −sin 10°.
Therefore sin 50° − sin 70° + sin 10° = −sin 10° + sin 10° = 0 = R.H.S.

questions.question: cos(π − θ) is equal to:
questions.explanation: cos(π − θ) = cos 180° cos θ + sin 180° sin θ = (−1)cos θ + 0 = −cos θ.

questions.question: tan(π + θ) is equal to:
questions.explanation: Tangent has period π, so tan(π + θ) = tan θ. (Expansion: (0 + tan θ)/(1 − 0·tan θ) = tan θ.)
questions.optionsRaw: a) tan θ  b) −cot θ  c) - tan θ  d) cot θ

questions.question: cos(2π + θ) is equal to:
questions.explanation: Cosine has period 2π, so cos(2π + θ) = cos θ. (Expansion: cos 2π cos θ − sin 2π sin θ = cos θ.)

If α, β and γ are the angles of ΔABC, then sin(α + β) is equal to:
questions.explanation: In ΔABC, α + β + γ = 180°, so α + β = 180° − γ. Hence sin(α + β) = sin(180° − γ) = sin γ.
questions.optionsRaw: a) sin γ  b) −sin γ  c) cos γ  d) −cos γ

questions.question: cos 2α is equal to:
questions.explanation: All three forms are valid: cos 2α = cos²α − sin²α = 2cos²α − 1 = 1 − 2sin²α, using sin²α + cos²α = 1.
questions.optionsRaw: a) cos²α − sin²α  b) 2cos²α − 1  c) 1 − 2 sin²α  d) all of these

questions.question: sin(α/2) is equal to:
questions.explanation: From cos α = 1 − 2sin²(α/2), we get sin²(α/2) = (1 − cos α)/2, so sin(α/2) = ±√((1 − cos α)/2). The sign is fixed by the quadrant of α/2.

questions.question: Solve the right angled triangle ABC in which γ = 90°, given a = 4 m, b = 3 m.
questions.explanation: γ = 90°, so c is the hypotenuse and a, b are the legs. By Pythagoras: c = √(a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>) = √(4<sup>2</sup> + 3<sup>2</sup>) = √25 = 5 m. tan α = a/b = 4/3 = 1.3333 ⇒ α = tan<sup>−1</sup>(1.3333) = 53.13° = 53°8′. β = 90° − α = 90° − 53.13° = 36.87° = 36°52′. (Printed key: α = 53°7′, β = 36°53′.)
questions.figure: Right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at C (γ = 90°); a = BC = 4 m, b = CA = 3 m, c = AB = 5 m.

questions.question: A vertical stick 16 m long casts a 12 cm long shadow. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
questions.answer: θ ≈ 53°8′ (taking the shadow as 12 m, as the printed key does).
questions.explanation: Let θ be the angle of elevation. In the right triangle formed by the stick and its shadow, tan θ = height/shadow = 16/12 = 1.3333 ⇒ θ = tan<sup>−1</sup>(1.3333) = 53.13° = 53°8′. Note: the shadow is printed as 12 cm, which is a misprint for 12 m — the printed key (53°7′) comes from 16/12. With a 12 cm shadow the angle would be tan<sup>−1</sup>(16/0.12) = tan<sup>−1</sup>(133.3) ≈ 89.57°.
questions.figure: Right triangle: vertical stick 16 m, horizontal shadow 12 m, angle of elevation θ of the sun at the shadow tip.

questions.question: Find the distance of a man from the foot of a tower 169 m high, if the angle of depression of the man from its top is 48°30′.
questions.explanation: The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation of the top from the man (alternate angles), so in the right triangle tan 48°30′ = 169/x ⇒ x = 169/tan 48°30′ = 169/1.13029 = 149.5 m.
questions.figure: Right triangle: vertical tower 169 m, horizontal distance x from its foot to the man, angle 48°30′ at the man.

questions.question: A string of a flying kite is 200 metres long and its angle of elevation is 58°30′. Find the height of the kite when the string is fully stretched.
questions.explanation: In the right triangle, the string is the hypotenuse and the height h is opposite the angle of elevation: sin 58°30′ = h/200 ⇒ h = 200 sin 58°30′ = 200(0.85264) = 170.53 m.
questions.figure: Right triangle: string 200 m as hypotenuse, vertical height h of the kite, angle 58°30′ at the ground.

questions.question: A man 1.8 m tall observes that the angle of elevation of the top of a tree at a distance of 12 m from him is 31°45′. What is the height of the tree?
questions.answer: Height of the tree ≈ 9.23 m (key: 9.22 m).
questions.explanation: Height of the tree above the man’s eye level = 12 tan 31°45′ = 12(0.61882) = 7.43 m. Adding the height of the man: height of tree = 7.43 + 1.8 = 9.23 m.
questions.figure: Right triangle: horizontal distance 12 m from the man’s eye to the tree, height above eye level h, angle 31°45′.

questions.question: From the top of a cliff 80 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is 12°30′. How far is the boat from the cliff?
questions.explanation: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation of the cliff top from the boat, so tan 12°30′ = 80/x ⇒ x = 80/tan 12°30′ = 80/0.22169 = 360.86 ≈ 361 m.
questions.figure: Right triangle: vertical cliff 80 m, horizontal distance x of the boat from the foot of the cliff, angle 12°30′ at the boat.

questions.question: Two masts are 20 m and 12 m high. If the line joining their tops makes an angle of 35° with the horizontal, find the distance between them.
questions.explanation: Difference in heights = 20 − 12 = 8 m. The line joining the tops, the horizontal through the shorter mast’s top and the vertical drop form a right triangle: tan 35° = 8/d ⇒ d = 8/tan 35° = 8/0.70021 = 11.43 ≈ 11.4 m.
questions.figure: Two vertical masts 20 m and 12 m high standing on the same horizontal ground, horizontal distance d apart; the segment joining their tops makes 35° with the horizontal.

questions.question: A window washer is working in a hotel building. An observer at a distance of 20 m from the building finds the angle of elevation of the worker to be 30°. The worker climbs up 12 m and the observer moves 4 m further away from the building. Find the new angle of elevation of the worker.
questions.explanation: First position: height of the worker above the observer’s eye = 20 tan 30° = 20(0.57735) = 11.547 m. After climbing 12 m the height becomes 11.547 + 12 = 23.547 m, and the observer is now 20 + 4 = 24 m away. tan θ = 23.547/24 = 0.98113 ⇒ θ = tan<sup>−1</sup>(0.98113) = 44.45° = 44°27′.
questions.figure: Two right triangles with a common vertical wall: observer 20 m then 24 m from the building, worker 11.547 m then 23.547 m above eye level.

Find the largest angle of ΔABC when a = 6 cm, b = 8 cm and c = 9.4 cm.
questions.explanation: The largest angle lies opposite the largest side, so it is γ (opposite c = 9.4 cm). cos γ = (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> − c<sup>2</sup>)/(2ab) = (36 + 64 − 88.36)/(2 × 6 × 8) = 11.64/96 = 0.12125 ⇒ γ = 83.03°.

questions.question: Find the smallest angle in ΔABC when a = 25 cm, b = 18 cm and c = 21 cm.
questions.explanation: The smallest angle is opposite the smallest side, so it is β (opposite b = 18 cm). cos β = (a<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>)/(2ac) = (625 + 441 − 324)/(2 × 25 × 21) = 742/1050 = 0.70667 ⇒ β = 45.0°.

questions.question: Find the length of the third side of a triangular building that faces 13.6 metres along one street and 13 metres along another street. The angle of intersection between the streets measures 72°.
If one side of a triangle is y units long, another side is 3 times as long and the angle between the two sides measures 35°, find the measures of the other two angles and the third side.
questions.answer: Third side ≈ 2.25y; the other angles are ≈ 15° and ≈ 130°.
questions.explanation: Third side: x<sup>2</sup> = y<sup>2</sup> + (3y)<sup>2</sup> − 2(y)(3y)cos 35° = y<sup>2</sup>(10 − 6(0.81915)) = 5.0851y<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x = 2.255y ≈ 2.25y. By the law of sines, the angle A opposite the side y satisfies sin A = y sin 35°/x = 0.57358/2.255 = 0.25437 ⇒ A = 14.74° ≈ 15°. The remaining angle = 180° − 35° − 14.74° = 130.26° ≈ 130°.

questions.question: If the length of larger side of a parallelogram is 55 cm and one diagonal of the parallelogram makes angles of measure 30° and 50° with a pair of adjacent sides, find the length of the diagonal.
questions.explanation: The diagonal cuts the parallelogram into a triangle whose angles at the two ends of the diagonal are 30° and 50°, so the third angle is 180° − 30° − 50° = 100°. The 55 cm side lies opposite the larger of 30° and 50°, i.e. opposite 50°. By the law of sines: d/sin 100° = 55/sin 50° ⇒ d = 55 sin 100°/sin 50° = 55(0.98481)/0.76604 = 70.71 cm.
questions.figure: Parallelogram with larger side 55 cm; the diagonal makes 30° with one adjacent side and 50° with the other, forming a triangle with angles 30°, 50°, 100°.

questions.question: The sides of a parallelogram are 25 cm and 35 cm long and one of its angles is 36°. Find the lengths of its diagonals.
questions.explanation: For a parallelogram with sides p, q and included angle θ the diagonals are d<sub>1</sub> = √(p<sup>2</sup> + q<sup>2</sup> + 2pq cos θ) and d<sub>2</sub> = √(p<sup>2</sup> + q<sup>2</sup> − 2pq cos θ). d<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = 625 + 1225 + 2(25)(35)(0.80902) = 1850 + 1415.8 = 3265.8 ⇒ d<sub>1</sub> = 57.15 cm. d<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1850 − 1415.8 = 434.2 ⇒ d<sub>2</sub> = 20.84 cm.

questions.question: Two hikers start from the same point; one walks 9 km heading east, the other one 10 km heading 55° north east. How far apart are they at the end of their walks?
questions.explanation: The two paths enclose 55°, so the distance d between the hikers is the third side of a triangle with sides 9 and 10: d<sup>2</sup> = 9<sup>2</sup> + 10<sup>2</sup> − 2(9)(10)cos 55° = 81 + 100 − 180(0.57358) = 181 − 103.24 = 77.76 ⇒ d = 8.818 km.

questions.question: Two planes start from Karachi International Airport at the same time and fly in directions that make an angle of 127° with each other. Their speeds are 525 km/h. How far apart are they at the end of 2 hours of flying time?
questions.explanation: Distance flown by each plane = 525 × 2 = 1050 km. By the law of cosines d<sup>2</sup> = 1050<sup>2</sup> + 1050<sup>2</sup> − 2(1050)(1050)cos 127° = 2(1050<sup>2</sup>)(1 − cos 127°) = 2205000(1.60182) = 3532013 ⇒ d = 1879.4 km.

questions.question: Find the area of triangle ABC when a = 8.6, b = 11.4, γ = 90°.
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle: ▲ = ½ab sin γ = ½(8.6)(11.4) sin 90° = ½(98.04)(1) = 49.02 square units.

questions.question: Find the area of triangle ABC when b = 63, c = 17, α = 120°.
questions.explanation: The included angle between b and c is α: ▲ = ½bc sin α = ½(63)(17) sin 120° = 535.5(0.86603) = 463.76 square units. (Printed key: 463.74.)

questions.question: Find the area of triangle ABC when c = 5.34, a = 9.30, β = 53°34′.
questions.explanation: The included angle between a and c is β: ▲ = ½ac sin β = ½(9.30)(5.34) sin 53°34′ = 24.831(0.80489) = 19.98 square units.

questions.question: Find the area of triangle ABC when c = 36, α = 46°, β = 66°.
questions.explanation: One side and two angles: γ = 180° − 46° − 66° = 68°, and ▲ = ½c<sup>2</sup> sin α sin β/sin γ = ½(36)<sup>2</sup>(sin 46°)(sin 66°)/sin 68° = 648(0.71934)(0.91355)/0.92718 = 459.28 square units. (Printed key: 459.22.)

The measures of the two sides of a triangle are 4 and 5 units. Find the third side so that the area of the triangle is 6 square units.
questions.answer: Third side = 3 units (or √73 ≈ 8.54 units if the included angle is obtuse).
questions.explanation: ▲ = ½(4)(5) sin θ = 10 sin θ = 6 ⇒ sin θ = 0.6 ⇒ θ = 36.87°. Then x<sup>2</sup> = 4<sup>2</sup> + 5<sup>2</sup> − 2(4)(5)cos 36.87° = 41 − 40(0.8) = 9 ⇒ x = 3 units. The obtuse possibility θ = 143.13° gives x<sup>2</sup> = 41 + 32 = 73, x = √73 ≈ 8.54 units. (Printed key: 3.)

questions.question: Find the area of the equilateral triangle whose each side is x units long.
questions.explanation: For an equilateral triangle the included angle between two sides is 60°, so ▲ = ½(x)(x) sin 60° = ½x<sup>2</sup>(√3/2) = (√3/4)x<sup>2</sup> square units. (Hero’s formula with s = 3x/2 gives the same result.)
